newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila overnight money slips in liquid market.
newsitem.headline: Manila overnight money slips in liquid market.

text.p: * Central Bank keeps overnight borrowing rate at 10.5 pct
Manila overnight money slipped to an average of 10.53125 percent on Friday from 10.5625 amid a liquid market, traders said.
Banks have little requirements since this is the end of the reserve week, they said.
Done rates were in a tight band from 10.635 to 10.53125 percent. The market had 24 lenders and 21 borrowers.
Volume had risen to 9.776 billion from 7.611 billion pesos.
Dealers said interest rates would move sideways since the Central Bank had not changed its borrowing rates despite the high liquidity in the market.
"The yield curve is flat. Nobody wants to take a long-term view," a foreign bank dealer said.
As a consequence, banks' buying focus in the secondary market continued to be on short-term bills to park their excess liquidity, traders said.
Banks gave bids of 10.665 to 10.75 percent on the three-month bills, according to a Reuter poll of nine institutions.
